verdict.rationale: Mastra is a TypeScript framework where tools are defined via createTool() with zod-based inputSchema/outputSchema, and structured output enforces a schema shape, plus workflow steps are described as 'type-safe logic' — giving strong compile-time and runtime schema validation for agent-authored code. However, the evidence never explicitly frames this as an agent 'catching its own mistakes at build time' (e.g., no mention of tsc/strict mode enforcement flow, IDE feedback loop, or independent hands-on confirmation of this build-time self-correction benefit). missing for 10: explicit build-time error-catching workflow evidence, independent/hands-on corroboration of typing catching agent mistakes, TypeScript strict-mode configuration details.
